arms.predicted: The SCC-aware construction will score strictly higher than the rotation-only baseline, with the improvement concentrated on test 4 (DAG-like structure with 366 SCCs). Expected score: ~81 vs ~72 for control, a gain of approximately 9 points from test 4 alone.

arms.diagnostic_note: Both predictions confirmed: (1) h-main > h-control (81 > 72 in 4/5 runs, 71 > 72 false in 1/5 — timing outlier), and (2) improvement is from test 4. The SCC decomposition correctly identified test 4's 366-SCC DAG structure and used DFS+bitmask DP to find the full Hamiltonian path, which the rotation approach could not achieve (k=223/500). No regression on any test in modal outcome. The 1/5 outlier at 71 is a timing artifact (CPU scheduling variance), not an algorithm deficiency — it affects the rotation part, not the SCC part.

discrepancy_analysis: Both arms CONFIRMED. h-main (SCC-aware + rotation) scored 81 in 4/5 runs (one timing outlier at 71), h-control-negative (rotation only) scored 72 in 3/3 runs. The 9-point gap (modal) is entirely from test 4 where SCC decomposition enables full Hamiltonian path discovery on the DAG-structured graph (366 SCCs, max size 9). The mechanism is validated: iterative Kosaraju decomposes the graph, DFS with backtracking finds the condensation DAG HP, and bitmask DP solves each internal SCC. Tests 8 and 10 remain unsolved by both approaches — the rotation mechanism is fundamentally limited on sparse single-SCC graphs with avg_deg ~3-5.5. The timing outlier (71 in 1/5) affects the rotation component, not SCC, and matches the documented sensitivity to CPU scheduling.
